faq.a: The holes in the arms point at an angle. As water shoots out one way, it pushes the arm the other way, so the arm spins without any motor of its own.
asks: What makes the spray arms turn?

faq.q: How does a dishwasher clean dishes?
faq.a: Hot water, strong detergent and powerful jets work together. The detergent breaks down grease and food, and the jets wash it away, again and again.
asks: What is the cycle of a dishwasher?

faq.a: Rinse aid makes water spread into thin sheets that slide off instead of forming drops, so dishes dry faster without spots.
asks: Why do glasses have spots after the dishwasher?

faq.q: Why does a dishwasher need salt?
faq.a: In hard-water areas, salt recharges a softener that removes calcium from the water, stopping white limescale marks on glasses.

faq.q: Does a dishwasher use more water than washing by hand?
faq.a: Usually not. A modern dishwasher uses around 10 litres for a full load because it recycles the same water, while washing by hand often uses much more.
asks: Is a dishwasher better for the environment?

facts: A modern full-size dishwasher typically uses about 9 to 12 litres of water per cycle.
Dishwasher spray arms are turned by the reaction push of their own angled water jets.
